findings.title: Alias-keyed pool survives test DB rename; tests can hit production DB
findings.suggested_fix: Make the PostgreSQL _nodb_cursor() fallback bypass the pool (e.g. build the fallback wrapper with OPTIONS={**self.settings_dict['OPTIONS'], 'pool': False}, or with alias=NO_DB_ALIAS). Also add a defensive self.connection.close_pool() in DatabaseCreation before settings_dict['NAME'] is rewritten (override create_test_db/_create_test_db as _clone_test_db/_destroy_test_db already do). Assumption: keying the pool by alias stays the design. Otherwise, rebuild the pool when get_connection_params() no longer matches pool.kwargs.
findings.first_evidence: django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:208 -- if self.alias not in self._connection_pools:

findings.title: Docs say pool option ignored on psycopg2, code raises
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docs sentence to: 'This option requires psycopg[pool] or psycopg-pool to be installed and raises ImproperlyConfigured with psycopg2.' Assumption: raising is the intended behavior, as the test asserts.
findings.first_evidence: docs/ref/databases.txt:270-271 -- This option requires ``psycopg[pool]`` or :pypi:`psycopg-pool` to be installed and is ignored with ``psycopg2``.

findings.title: Pool dict with configure/check/kwargs/open crashes with TypeError
findings.suggested_fix: Before constructing the pool, reject the reserved keys with a clear error. For example: reserved = {'kwargs', 'open', 'configure', 'check'} & pool_options.keys(); if reserved: raise ImproperlyConfigured(f"OPTIONS['pool'] cannot set {sorted(reserved)}."). Alternatively, chain a user-supplied configure after self._configure_connection. Assumption: rejecting the keys is acceptable for 5.1.

findings.title: init_connection_state no longer calls ensure_timezone/ensure_role methods
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the per-connection logic as overridable methods that take a connection, such as _configure_timezone(self, connection) and _configure_role(self, connection), and call them from _configure_connection. Keep ensure_role() as a thin wrapper around self._configure_role(self.connection) for compatibility. Assumption: backward compatibility for backend subclasses is required.

residual_risks: Parallel test runs with fork: setup_worker_connection() (base creation.py:377-384) updates NAME and calls connection.close() but not close_pool(). If the parent reopens the 'default' pool after _clone_test_db (e.g. during run_checks before run_suite), forked workers inherit the parent's pool and sockets and connect to the main test DB, not their clone. I did not confirm that anything reconnects in the parent between cloning and forking.
Pooled connections are returned without a reset callback, so session state set by user code (SET search_path, SET TIME ZONE, SET ROLE overrides) carries over to the next checkout in another request.

The code relies on psycopg_pool>=3.2 (the check= kwarg and ConnectionPool.check_connection), but only tests/requirements pins it. The docs give no minimum version, and an older psycopg_pool would fail with TypeError/AttributeError, not ImproperlyConfigured. This is based on the psycopg_pool changelog; only 3.3.3 was available to inspect locally.

close_pool() reads self.pool, which creates a pool if none exists. A concurrent close_pool() and get_new_connection() can also race: if open() is called on a pool that is closed but not yet removed, it raises PoolClosed, and a second del raises KeyError. In practice this mostly affects tests.
testing_gaps: No test covers test-database creation with pooling when the 'postgres' DB is inaccessible (the _nodb_cursor fallback path). No test asserts that connections after create_test_db use the test NAME rather than a pool created earlier.

findings.title: Shared ensure_connection guard wedges non-autocommit connections; untested
findings.suggested_fix: Add a backend-agnostic regression test in tests/transactions/tests.py (NonAutocommitTests or similar): set_autocommit(False); with transaction.atomic(): connection.close(); then assert a later cursor().execute('SELECT 1') succeeds (skip in-memory SQLite, whose close() is a no-op). To make it pass, clear the stale atomic state when the outermost autocommit-disabled block drops a closed connection. In django/db/transaction.py's `elif not connection.savepoint_ids and not connection.commit_on_exit:` branch, also set `connection.in_atomic_block = False` next to `connection.connection = None`, so the guard only fires while still inside a live atomic block. This assumes the guard is meant only for re-opening inside an active block, as with the pooled _close.

findings.title: Atomic-block guard test never exercises pooled close path
findings.suggested_fix: Drive the real path: with pool set to {"min_size": 0, "max_size": 1} on no_pool_connection(alias="default_pool"), enter transaction.atomic(using=new_connection.alias) or set new_connection.in_atomic_block through set_autocommit(False) + atomic on the wrapper, run a query, call new_connection.close(), assert new_connection.connection is None, then assert ProgrammingError on the next cursor(). Clean up with close_pool() in finally. If the wrapper is not registered in `connections`, drive it with new_connection.set_autocommit(False) and the Atomic context manager patched to use the wrapper.
findings.first_evidence: tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py:334-337 -- new_connection.in_atomic_block = True / new_connection.closed_in_transaction = True / with self.assertRaisesMessage(ProgrammingError, msg): new_connection.ensure_connection()

findings.title: Timezone pool test bypasses ensure_timezone close_pool path
findings.suggested_fix: Create the pool before the override and leave an idle connection in it: set pool to {"min_size": 0, "max_size": 1}, open a cursor, SHOW TIMEZONE, then close() (back to the pool). Then call new_connection.ensure_timezone() directly, or temporarily register the wrapper with connections["default_pool"] so self.settings(TIME_ZONE=...) reaches it, instead of `del new_connection.timezone_name`. Assert the next cursor reports the new zone. Add a case where a connection is checked out during the override, to cover the `connection._pool.putconn` path in _close().

findings.title: psycopg2 test pins a raise that docs call 'ignored'
findings.suggested_fix: Assuming raising is the intended contract (it matches the code and assertion), change docs/ref/databases.txt:271 to say the option requires psycopg 3 and raises ImproperlyConfigured with psycopg2, and rename the test to test_connect_pool_setting_raises_for_psycopg2. If ignoring is intended instead, drop the raise in get_connection_params() and assert the connection opens without a pool.

residual_risks: No settings or CI config in the repo runs the suite with OPTIONS['pool'] enabled (grep for 'pool' in .github/, tests/*.py, tox.ini found nothing relevant). Pool-only production branches therefore run only if an external CI job sets the option: close_pool() in _clone_test_db/_destroy_test_db, the close_if_health_check_failed short-circuit, and the django_test_skips pool entries. That could not be verified offline.
No PostgreSQL server was available, so the new pool tests in tests/backends/postgresql/tests.py were not executed. Their pass/fail behavior is inferred from reading the code.

With psycopg2 and OPTIONS['pool'] set, ensure_timezone() -> close_pool() -> self.pool -> get_connection_params() raises ImproperlyConfigured, so override_settings(TIME_ZONE=...) would raise from the setting_changed handler. No test covers this.
testing_gaps: assume_role with a pool: _configure_connection runs as the pool configure callback, but test_connect_role was switched to no_pool_connection(), so no test checks that SET ROLE is applied to pooled connections.
isolation_level with a pool: test_connect_isolation_level now uses no_pool_connection(), so the pooled get_new_connection path that sets connection.isolation_level after getconn() has no test.

close_if_health_check_failed() returning early for pooled connections, and is_usable() returning False when self.connection is None, are new branches with no direct test. The pool skips in features.py turn off the existing health-check tests under pool settings without adding a replacement.

DatabaseCreation._clone_test_db/_destroy_test_db calling close_pool() has no mock-based test in tests/backends/postgresql/test_creation.py, for example asserting close_pool is called before the CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE runs.

findings.title: Per-alias pool keeps stale NAME after test DB rename
findings.suggested_fix: In DatabaseWrapper._nodb_cursor's fallback, construct the throwaway wrapper with alias=NO_DB_ALIAS (the pool property already returns None for it) so the fallback never seeds the alias pool. Also add close_pool() after settings rewrites in the PostgreSQL creation class: override create_test_db (or _create_test_db) to call self.connection.close_pool() before NAME is switched, and override setup_worker_connection to call self.connection.close_pool() before delegating, matching the existing _clone_test_db/_destroy_test_db pattern. Assumption: callers never intend a pool to outlive a settings_dict change.

findings.title: Docs say pool ignored on psycopg2, code raises
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docs sentence to 'This option requires ``psycopg[pool]`` or :pypi:`psycopg-pool` to be installed and raises ImproperlyConfigured with ``psycopg2``.' and rename the test to test_connect_pool_setting_raises_for_psycopg2. Assumption: raising is the intended behavior; if 'ignored' is intended, drop the raise in get_connection_params instead.

findings.title: Default pool config hands out unchecked idle connections
findings.suggested_fix: Document under 'Connection pool' that CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS controls the pool's check callback, and fix the comment at line 503 to say 'The pool performs health checks itself when CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS is enabled.' Alternative: let OPTIONS['pool']['check'] override, defaulting to ConnectionPool.check_connection when pooling.

residual_risks: Parallel test workers under fork: setup_worker_connection rewrites settings_dict NAME to the clone but does not close the inherited class-level _connection_pools entry. If the parent opens a pool on an alias after the last _clone_test_db (which closes it) and before forking, workers would reuse a pool whose dbname is the parent test DB, whose idle sockets are shared with the parent, and whose worker threads did not survive the fork. I could not confirm whether the parent connects between cloning and forking (no live PostgreSQL).

Fail-slow under DB outage: with pooling, getconn() waits for the psycopg_pool timeout (default 30s) while background reconnect attempts fail, then raises PoolTimeout. Without a pool, connection-refused or auth errors (including a bad assume_role, now applied in the pool configure callback) surface immediately. Each request thread can block up to 30s, and the root cause is only in logs. Behavior inferred from psycopg_pool 3.3.3 source; not exercised live.

pool=True uses ConnectionPool defaults (min_size=4, max_size=4), which caps each process at 4 concurrent DB-using requests. Further requests queue, then fail with PoolTimeout. Docs do not mention sizing relative to worker/thread counts.
testing_gaps: No test covers create_test_db (or the _nodb_cursor fallback) with OPTIONS['pool'] set to assert that connections after setup target the test database name rather than a previously cached pool.

residual_risks: Session state now outlives the request when pooling is on (django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:305, 284-298). With pool enabled, CONN_MAX_AGE must be 0, which used to mean a fresh connection with assume_role and the time zone applied on every request. Now _configure_connection runs only once, when psycopg_pool opens a physical connection (configure=self._configure_connection), and init_connection_state skips it ('if self.connection is not None and not self.pool'). putconn() only rolls back an open transaction (psycopg_pool/pool.py:790-815) and no reset callback is set. Any session-level change made by app code is therefore handed to the next request that borrows the connection. That covers raw SET ROLE/RESET ROLE, set_config(..., false) GUCs used for RLS tenant scoping, temp tables, and advisory locks. This matches existing CONN_MAX_AGE>0 behavior, so it is not a regression. The new docs section (docs/ref/databases.txt 'Connection pool') does not mention it.

If a user passes a 'reset' callable in OPTIONS['pool'] (forwarded via **pool_options) that runs DISCARD ALL / SET SESSION AUTHORIZATION DEFAULT, the connection drops assume_role and runs as the login role. The pool never runs configure again on reuse, so later queries run with the login role's privileges. This happens only if the user supplies such a reset function, which the diff does not do.
testing_gaps: No test covers OPTIONS['assume_role'] together with OPTIONS['pool']. test_connect_role was switched to no_pool_connection(), so nothing checks that the pool configure callback actually applies SET ROLE to pooled connections. Nothing checks that a configure failure (nonexistent role) surfaces as an error rather than serving a connection under the login role. Suggested test: a pooled connection with assume_role set to an existing role should report it from SELECT current_user; with a nonexistent role, getconn should fail.

findings.title: Pool configure with assume_role re-enters Django wrapper from pool worker
findings.suggested_fix: In ensure_role(), build the statement without the Django wrapper, e.g. `from psycopg import sql; cursor.execute(sql.SQL("SET ROLE {}").format(sql.Literal(role_name)))` (or `psycopg.ClientCursor(connection).mogrify("SET ROLE %s", [role_name])` on the raw psycopg connection passed to the callback). Keep `ops.compose_sql` only on the non-pool path if psycopg2 compatibility is needed (pooling is psycopg3-only). Add a pooled variant of test_connect_role.
findings.first_evidence: django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:103 -- sql = ops.compose_sql("SET ROLE %s", [role_name])  (called from _configure_connection at base.py:280, registered as ConnectionPool(configure=self._configure_connection) at base.py:161)

findings.title: Test DB NAME switch ignored by pre-existing pool; tests hit real DB
findings.suggested_fix: In postgresql/creation.py, override _create_test_db() (or create_test_db()) to call self.connection.close_pool() before delegating, so the pool is rebuilt after the NAME switch. Also override setup_worker_connection() to discard any inherited pool without closing its shared sockets (e.g. `self.connection._connection_pools.pop(self.connection.alias, None)` before super()). More robust option: key _connection_pools on (alias, os.getpid()) and on the frozen connect kwargs' dbname, or assert pool.kwargs['dbname'] matches settings_dict['NAME'] in get_new_connection.
findings.first_evidence: django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:154-164 -- connect_kwargs = self.get_connection_params() ... pool = ConnectionPool(kwargs=connect_kwargs, ...)  (stored once in class-level _connection_pools[self.alias])

findings.title: Threads exiting without close() permanently consume pool slots
findings.suggested_fix: At minimum, document in docs/ref/databases.txt (Connection pool section) that connections used outside the request/response cycle must be closed (connection.close() / close_old_connections()) or the pool will be exhausted. Optionally, in get_new_connection() when pooled, register `weakref.finalize(self, pool.putconn, connection)` and detach it in _close(), so the connection returns to the pool when the wrapper is garbage-collected (assumes putconn from a GC context is acceptable; pool reset rolls back open transactions).
findings.first_evidence: django/db/backends/postgresql/base.py:228 -- connection = self.pool.getconn()  (only returned via _close(): self.connection._pool.putconn(self.connection) at base.py:294)

residual_risks: Health checks are off by default with pool=True (check=None unless CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS), and close_if_health_check_failed() is bypassed. Previously CONN_MAX_AGE=0 meant a fresh connection per request. Now, after a DB restart/failover or a middlebox idle timeout shorter than the pool's max_idle (10 min), each stale pooled connection fails one request before it is discarded.

Parallel test runner with fork start method: if the parent opens a pooled connection after the last _clone_test_db (e.g. a system check that reads a pg_version-dependent feature), children inherit an opened pool (dead worker threads, shared sockets, dbname of the template DB). setup_worker_connection does not discard it. I did not confirm whether stock run_checks opens a connection.

close_pool() is unsynchronised (check self.pool, close, then `del self._connection_pools[alias]`) and ensure_timezone() now closes the process-wide pool. This is reachable in tests via override_settings(TIME_ZONE/USE_TZ). Concurrent callers (e.g. live-server threads) can hit a KeyError, or a closed pool between get_new_connection's two self.pool lookups (open() on a closed pool raises).
testing_gaps: No test runs pool=True together with assume_role (test_connect_role is forced to pool=False via no_pool_connection), which would have caught the configure-callback re-entry.
No test covers create_test_db (or setup_worker_connection) when a pool for the alias already exists with a different NAME.

findings.title: Docs say pool option ignored with psycopg2 but code raises
findings.suggested_fix: Align docs with get_connection_params(): state that OPTIONS['pool'] requires psycopg 3 and raises ImproperlyConfigured with psycopg2.
